response.rationale: The specification provides a legal name for the food: 'Chicken soup with vegetables', which is a descriptive name and not just a brand or fancy name. This satisfies the requirement for a legal, customary, or descriptive name. For the QUID requirement, the ingredients 'Chicken stock', 'Chicken', 'Carrots', and 'Leeks' all appear in the name or are essential to characterise the food, and their percentages are clearly declared in the ingredient list (e.g., Chicken stock 52%, Chicken 18%, Carrots 11%, Leeks 7%). This meets the requirement for quantitative indication of ingredients as set out in Art. 22(1).

citations.quoted_span: The indication of the quantity of an ingredient or category of ingredients used in the manufacture or preparation of a food shall be required where the ingredient or category of ingredients concerned: (a) appears in the name of the food or is usually associated with that name by the consumer; (b) is emphasised on the labelling in words, pictures or graphics; or (c) is essential to characterise a food and to distinguish it from products with which it might be confused because of its name or appearance.

In the case of meat products and meat preparations which have the appearance of a cut, joint, slice, portion or carcase of meat, the name of the food shall include an indication of the presence of added water if the added water makes up more than 5 % of the weight of the finished product.
